chapter: Danny's rise through New York bands to Cab Calloway
title: Suppressed Black talent and the novelty vaudeville acts
summary: Danny says Black talent was held back, recalling vibraphone dancers, hoop jugglers and the counting chicken.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Okay. So I can see why these people had...you know, kept... Don't let too many of them. Because if you let all the Negroes with talent out there, there would be nothing for them other people to do. I mean, (?) all them millions of Chinamens out there. They got some Negroes who can do some strange things. Like that boy who dance them on vibraphones and make music. Isn't that something? What was his name? Had a whole keyboard, he did that tap dance, would sing that song.
Yeah, sure! I can't think of his...

Made the news. There were ...(?)... people like that. They tell me they had a hoop act one time, a cat made six hoops, and they told me he'd stand by the wings and he'd throw these hoops out, and them hoops did all kinds of things on the stage. And they almost bumped into one another, and they moved out. They said, "How do you control them hoops and made 'em do that?" There was a guy who would take a chicken on the stage and talk to the chicken, and the chicken followed. He says, "Count me to five," the chicken says, "CLUCK-CLUCK-CLUCK-CLUCK-CLUCK," and the chicken count... All kinds of fantastic acts.
See, if you let them... If people would let everybody who could do something... That's why so many of us had to die... By being so innovative, we had to die on the vine.
What was that guy's name who used to be able to dance on them skates, who was so great?
Yeah, yeah...! He was strange, too. He used to do some things that would entertain you off the stage and on the stage. So many of them.
